liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Queen Jane Approximately** (1 review): Reviewer says the stretch from Queen Jane Approximately through Terrapin Station is especially strong [8]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): Bird Song is described as truly taking flight and reaching epic proportions [10]
- **Fire on the Mountain** (1 review): Fire kept extending; reviewer checked the time and found half an hour had passed since Scarlet began [9]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Morning Dew is praised as an emotional performance that poured Jerry's soul out to the crowd [10]
- **U.S. Blues** (1 other source): U.S. Blues was the encore [1]

## The recordings

- **gd94-06-13.schoeps.pujol.8239.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 17 songs; 175 min; rated 3.5/5 by 20 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the recording too tinny to tolerate [18]
- **gd1994-06-13.145463.nak300.anastas.flac16**: source not stated; 16 songs; 175 min [3]. Said about its sound: Uploader finds it an upgrade over crisp FOB MK41 sources, with smooth classic Nak sound and plenty of low end [3]
- **gd1994-06-13.137718.sbd.pset2.flac1644**: soundboard; 6 songs; 75 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [6]
- **gd1994-06-13.152516.akg.fob.gibian-larson.flac1644**: source not stated; 16 songs; 178 min [2]

## Around the show

- Sound mix was adjusted over the first couple of songs, and was loud and good by Bird Song [9]
- Fans waited in rain before the show, and the cold breeze rose after dark [11]
- No video screens, elaborate lights or opening act; just the band in an old downtown stadium [11]
- The recording suggests an awkward outdoor venue, yet the band sounds like they were enjoying themselves [12]
- Reviewer's first Dead show at age 17; traveled from Montana, and also attended the Eugene shows the following week [13]
- Reviewer had no ticket; Seattle police were harsh, but hundreds danced outside where music carried clearly [14]
- Reviewer's run that summer went Cal Expo, then Seattle, then Eugene to Las Vegas [14]
- Venue was a few blocks from reviewer's home then; they also attended the following day's show [15]
- Reviewer ranks this Scarlet>Fire very near the best ever, among the best they saw live [9]
- Reviewer calls this the most under-appreciated show of 1994, possibly of the 1990s [10]
- Reviewer has heard better shows but still holds this one in affection [11]
- Reviewer, who dismisses post-1991 Dead, considers this one of the gems of 1994 [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd94-06-13.schoeps.pujol.8239.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Marc Pujol; source: Audience: Schoeps CMC441's [1]. Also: Recorded with Schoeps CMC441s front-of-board, then DAT, PC, WAV and SHN; seeded to etree by Marc Pujol [1]
- **gd1994-06-13.145463.nak300.anastas.flac16**: taped by John Anastas; source: Nakamichi CM300 > DAT [3]. Also: Master DAT from John Anastas's collection, patched from an unknown taper's Nak 300s deck tape [3]
- **gd1994-06-13.137718.sbd.pset2.flac1644**: taped by unknown; transferred by Chris Mrachek; source: Partial Set 2 Source: SBD > ? > DAT > CDR; CDR (TaiyoYuden 80m japan) > EAC (secure, 100% quality) > Audacity (edits, fades, levels) > CDWav (tracking) > TLH… [6]. Also: First circulating soundboard portion of this show, covering Scarlet Begonias through Space, from a source disc [6]
- **gd1994-06-13.152516.akg.fob.gibian-larson.flac1644**: taped by Tapes provided by Paul Gibian; transferred by Transfer by Chris Larson; source: AKG(fob):D [2]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Seattle Center Memorial Stadium - June 13, 1994](https://www.dead.net/show/june-13-1994) [20]
